Outcome: remove the ephemeral-port reservation gap from every positive fixture in tze_hud_runtime. The pinned runtime-wide inventory contains eight existing declarations: five MCP HTTP tests, two windowed gRPC tests and one headless gRPC test. Each fixture either lets the existing real MCP server own a port-zero listener and consumes its returned eager local_addr, or retains a real loopback listener continuously and transfers it exactly once into the same enabled gRPC service/accept implementation used by the production wrapper. Preserve every existing assertion and production bind behavior. Prove reliability with the original literal ten consecutive cargo test -p tze_hud_runtime --lib mcp runs while a genuine separate cargo build is compiling the same final source HEAD.

Authority: this is the existing P2 bug and all three original acceptance criteria, interpreted runtime-wide rather than limited to the five navigation hits. Current docs/scope.md T8/working rules, docs/vision.md and docs/invariants.md govern maintenance. The coordinator explicitly authorizes only narrow private enabled-start/owned-listener body extraction with cfg(test)-only fixture adapters for the three gRPC positives because their production port-zero sentinel must stay disabled. No new public listener API or prerequisite is required. Do not use pre-reset references as change authority.

Non-goals: no public API/production argument/config/env/default/feature/dependency change; no reinterpretation of gRPC port zero; no auth/permission/session/lease/budget/error/timing/policy changes; no new generic server abstraction, reconstructed service, fixed/random retry ports, semantic sleeps/polling, mirror/source-scan test, new test declaration, unrelated startup-wait removal or test deletion. Protected T7 code and the separate integration package's own port probes are outside the repair scope; existing callers still compile and execute their current gates. No standalone documentation or spec amendment. Expected declaration delta +0 ~8 -0.

Owned files: crates/tze_hud_runtime/src/mcp.rs (five test bodies/comments only), src/windowed/network.rs (two test bodies/comments plus the minimum private shared enabled-start seam), src/headless.rs (one test body/comments plus minimum private shared owned-listener serve seam). matches.title: Logical-dp sizing per monitor with a global ui.scale token
matches.description:
Outcome: every token size is a logical dp value, rendered at (monitor Windows scale factor x ui.scale) physical px on each monitor, so text and chrome are legible at the owner's 150% and the owner can enlarge everything with one token. Part of epic hud-h51u7.

Owner decision 2026-10-06: one global `ui.scale` design token (e.g. 1.25) multiplies every logical size on top of each monitor's Windows scale factor (owner runs 150%). No per-monitor scale overrides. Today text renders in physical px and looks too small at 150%; the owner said text should be at least 50% bigger (dp sizing alone gives 1.5x at 150%).

Today: everything is physical px. windowed/mod.rs:1222-1230 reads scale_factor() "for diagnostics only"; lifecycle.rs:2358-2363 says the same; no ScaleFactorChanged handling; no ui.scale anywhere. The only scale-like code is text.rs:1580 scale_portal_font_px (portals only) and the degradation texture scale. The hairline-border half of the old version of this bead moved to its own sibling bead.

Non-goals: per-monitor overrides; window sizing for mixed DPI (hud-670ds); restyling elements (restyle sub-epics).

Cold start: repo /home/orca/orca/projects/tze-hud. Read CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, docs/vision.md, docs/scope.md and docs/api.md first. Work in a worktree (scripts/worktree-add.sh .worktrees/<name> -b <branch>) off origin/main. Gates: `just ci`; GPU tests via `just test-gpu` (never bare cargo test -p tze_hud_compositor); Windows-only code via `just clippy-windows-gnu` plus Windows CI. Line numbers below are as of origin/main 788e5210 (or the PR #1336 branch where stated) and may drift.
matches.design:
- Token resolution stays logical: tokens.rs resolve_tokens (:1018) and themes.rs resolve_config_tokens are unchanged in meaning; sizes are dp.
- One seam applies the factor: policy_builder.rs build_effective_policy (:269) / token_f32 (:35) take a per-display `scale = monitor.scale_factor * ui.scale` and produce physical RenderingPolicy values (font_size_px, margins, outline_width, radii, slot geometry); compositor-side token readers (token_colors.rs resolvers, system_card.rs, safe_mode_overlay.rs, widget_geometry.rs drag handles, portal tokens) read through the same scaled view instead of raw px. Zones render per display after hud-1pt5h, so each zone uses its display's scale.
- Text cache key (compositor/src/text.rs:106) already includes px size, so different monitors get distinct entries.
- Widget SVGs rasterize at instance size x scale (crisp, not upscaled bitmaps).
- Hairlines: 1dp x scale, rounded, minimum 1 physical px.
- ui.scale: number token in [0.5, 3.0], default 1.0, set only in [design_tokens]. [decision] themes may not set ui.scale (a user preference, not a theme value): validate_theme rejects it. Reversible: yes.
- Handle WindowEvent::ScaleFactorChanged: re-derive that display's scale and rebuild its policies (no other wake).
- hud-h51u7.5 live reload re-applies ui.scale; keep the scale application a pure function it can call.
matches.acceptance_criteria:
1. CPU-level tests (no GPU): at scale_factor 1.5 and ui.scale 1.0, notification body/title sizes, padding and slot height in the built policy are 1.5x today's values; at ui.scale 1.25 they are 1.875x. Extend the nearest policy_builder / notification_layout tests rather than adding parallel suites.
2. Two displays with different scale factors produce different physical sizes for the same zone content (per-display policy test).
3. Hit regions (notification dismiss/actions, drag handles) scale with drawn geometry (extend an existing hit-region test).
4. A theme that sets ui.scale fails validation; [design_tokens] "ui.scale" = 1.25 is accepted; out-of-range values fail with the existing token error code.
5. `just token-footprint` and `just idle-efficiency-checker` unchanged.
6. docs/api.md design-token section documents dp units and ui.scale.
7. Before/after screenshot at 150% in the PR (owner host before; headless after at a simulated 1.5 scale).

matches.title: HUD visual redesign: semantic design-token foundation + per-element redesign (/th-design)
matches.description:
Why: HUD elements are visually inconsistent and partly off-system: drag handles ignore tokens (widget_geometry.rs:72,213-316), status-indicator SVG hardcodes 13 hex colours, notification rendering has ~15 hardcoded sizes/opacities (token_colors.rs:80-190, text.rs:556, zone_render.rs:302). Token families lack elevation, motion, state layers, line height, semantic surface roles. Owner wants a modern redesign (Material Design 3 / Ant / Polaris references).

What: (1) token foundation spec: semantic surface/on-surface roles with tonal elevation (renderer has no shadows/blur/gradients, so M3-style tonal surfaces), type scale, 4/8 spacing, shape, motion, state-layer tokens; (2) redesign each element against it: notification card, alert banner, subtitle, status bar, gauge/progress/status widgets, portal, pairing card, drag handles, safe-mode; (3) remove hardcodes. Iterate with user-test screenshot loop; owner signs off per element.
matches.design:
Owner decisions 2026-10-05: Tonal Glass direction approved (canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/7U7xiKxWGAptBz7GaqQ2DN). Design must be swappable: multiple themes selectable by user preference. Mechanism: a theme is a named, token-only layer (no layout logic) resolved canonical -> theme -> [design_tokens] overrides. Built-in themes ship in the exe (assets/themes/<name>.toml via include_str!: tonal-glass default, classic, blueprint); config selects one ([design_tokens] theme = "tonal-glass"). Sizes become logical dp scaled per monitor (after hud-1pt5h). Every element must render only from tokens so a theme can restyle all of it.

Owner decisions 2026-10-06:
- UI scale: one global `ui.scale` design token (e.g. 1.25) multiplies every logical size on top of each monitor's Windows scale factor (owner runs 150%). No per-monitor scale overrides. Lives with the logical-dp sizing bead hud-h51u7.3. Today text renders in physical px and is too small at 150%; text should be at least 50% bigger.
- Theme/font UX: config file with live reload (hud-h51u7.5) PLUS an in-HUD picker: a small settings card opened by a shortcut, for choosing theme and font. New UI surface: design pass on the canvas under the /th-design bar, then implementation; the choice persists to the config; agents never set themes (token-minimal rule); the shortcut must not collide with Ctrl+Shift+P (pairing) or Ctrl+Shift+F12 (safe mode).

Structure (2026-10-06 replan): closed .1 theme layer, .2 fonts, .6 blueprint; open .3 logical-dp + ui.scale, hairline SDF borders, .5 live reload, sub-epic .4 restyle zone elements, sub-epic restyle widgets and runtime chrome, sub-epic settings card picker, and a terminal reconciliation that depends on each sub-epic's reconciliation (epics cannot block tasks in this repo).
[decision] status-indicator themes (minimal/system/friendly): delete them in favour of theme tokens. Not an owner gate: docs/vision.md says themes are the owner's choice and models never choose them, and CLAUDE.md forbids styling payloads through model context, so a model-settable `theme` widget param contradicts the pillars. Implemented in the widgets restyle child. Reversible: yes.
matches.acceptance_criteria: Every listed element consumes only tokens (no hardcoded colours/sizes in render paths or widget SVGs); sizes are logical dp x monitor scale x ui.scale; theme and font switch live from the config file and from the in-HUD settings card, persisted to the config; before/after screenshots per element signed off by the owner per sub-epic; token-footprint gate unchanged except the documented status-indicator param removal (no styling via LLM surfaces).

matches.title: POC: acceptance gaps and demo
matches.description:
Close the gaps between the shipped app (tze_hud_app + production.toml) and docs/scope.md 'POC acceptance', prove each bullet with a headless end-to-end test in Linux CI, build a single demo agent, and run the checklist on the owner's Windows overlay.

Governing spec: docs/scope.md 'POC acceptance' (Portal, Zones, Widgets, Tiles, Override, Idle); docs/api.md; docs/invariants.md §1, §3, §4, §5, §9; docs/vision.md 'The real-estate lifecycle'.

Survey verdict (2026-10-03): Portal partial (never run end to end); Zones TTL/delay yes, action buttons never drawn; Widgets missing from the shipped artifact; Tiles partial (orphan badge never drawn, reap wipes same-namespace MCP content); Override no (no safe-mode entry, MCP bypasses safe mode, tiles/portals not dismissable); Idle partial (notification countdown and composer caret redraw at 60 fps).

## Success Criteria
1. tests/integration/poc_acceptance.rs proves every acceptance bullet except pixel/idle claims, headless in CI.
2. Safe mode and dismiss win over a hung agent on every surface (MCP, gRPC, portal).
3. The shipped exe has its widgets; a widget update re-rasterizes only that widget.
4. Static content on screen costs no frames between events.
5. examples/poc_demo drives zones, widgets, tiles and override against the live app.
6. The owner runs the full checklist on the Windows overlay and it passes.
matches.design:
Order: Wave A (independent fixes) and B1 (headless harness, T7's guard) first; then overlay behavior (B2-B8); then C1 (remaining acceptance tests), C2 demo, C3 Windows smoke; then human sign-off and the owner-host run.
Cohesion override: more than 9 children because the coordinator required one epic per area and the POC spans six independent acceptance bullets with distinct risk and sign-off gates.
Decisions (coordinator 2026-10-03): fix docs/api.md to say zone:notification-area (don't rename the zone); safe-mode global hotkey configurable, default Ctrl+Shift+F12, RegisterHotKey; tile/portal dismiss = token-styled close button on hover in chrome (visual sign-off is needs-human); 're-renders only that widget' = re-rasterizes only that widget's SVG, scope.md wording updated; resident tile agent gets its own agent entry (allow ["tiles"]) via pairing once T6 lands, tests use agents.toml injection; stale PRs #658 #659 #1193 #1216 #1218 #1219 already closed.
Gating rule: anything requiring a real Windows desktop/visual check, real install on the owner's host, or an owner taste call is a separate needs-human bead.
